conbody.p: SAML2 authenticationImpala can authenticate users with single sign-on (SSO) through the SAML2 browser profile. Impala acts as the service provider, and the users sign in at an external identity provider (IdP), for example Keycloak or Okta. You can enable SAML2 for the following endpoints of an impalad coordinator. Each endpoint has its own flags, and the endpoints share the other flags:

ul.li: The HiveServer2 HTTP endpoint (--hs2_http_port), for clients that connect with the hs2-http protocol. This is available since .
The coordinator Web UI. This is available starting in . See .

conbody.p: SAML2 authentication is available only on coordinators, and it requires TLS.

section.title: Registering Impala at the identity provider
section.p: Before you configure Impala, register it as a service provider at the IdP, and export the metadata file of the IdP. Impala uses the metadata file to validate the SAML responses. At the IdP, specify:

ul.li: The service provider entity ID. It must be the same as the value of --saml2_sp_entity_id. If you do not set the flag, each endpoint uses its callback URL as the entity ID.
The callback URL (the assertion consumer service URL) of the endpoint, the value of --saml2_sp_callback_url or --webserver_saml2_sp_callback_url.

section.p: Each endpoint has its own IdP metadata flag (--saml2_idp_metadata for the HiveServer2 HTTP endpoint and --webserver_saml2_idp_metadata for the Web UI) and its own callback URL, so the endpoints can use the same IdP or different IdPs.
If the endpoints use the same IdP, the entity ID determines the registration:

ul.li: If you do not set --saml2_sp_entity_id, the endpoints have different entity IDs, so register Impala as two service providers at the IdP, one for each endpoint, each with its own callback URL.
If you set --saml2_sp_entity_id, both endpoints use the same entity ID, so register Impala as one service provider with two assertion consumer service URLs, the callback URLs of the two endpoints.

section.title: Flags that are shared by the endpoints
section.p: Set the following impalad startup flags once for all the endpoints that use SAML2:

ul.li: --saml2_keystore_path: The path of the keystore that holds the key pair that Impala uses to sign the requests. If the file does not exist, Impala creates a keystore. You must set this flag.
--saml2_keystore_password_cmd: A command that prints the password of the keystore. You must set this flag.
--saml2_private_key_password_cmd: A command that prints the password of the private key in the keystore.
--saml2_sp_entity_id: The entity ID of the service provider. The default is the callback URL.

--saml2_want_assertations_signed: Whether Impala requires the assertions of the responses to be signed. The default is true. Set it to false only for testing, because it makes the authentication insecure.
--saml2_sign_requests: Whether Impala signs the SAML requests, so that the IdP can validate them. The default is false.

section.title: Restricting the access to groups
section.p: By default, Impala accepts every user that the IdP authenticates. To allow only the members of some groups, set --saml2_group_attribute_name to the name of the attribute in the SAML assertion that holds the groups, and set --saml2_group_filter to a comma-separated list of the allowed groups. If you set the attribute name, you must also set the filter. Only the users whose assertion has the attribute with a group from the list can sign in. The filter applies to every endpoint that uses SAML2.

section.title: SAML2 authentication on the HiveServer2 HTTP endpoint
section.p: To enable SAML2 on the HiveServer2 HTTP endpoint, start the coordinators with the following flags in addition to the shared flags and the flags that enable TLS for the client connections:

ul.li: --saml2_idp_metadata: The path of the metadata file of the IdP.

--saml2_sp_callback_url: The URL where the IdP posts the SAML responses, in the form https://host:port/path. Use the port of the HiveServer2 HTTP endpoint as the clients and the browser reach it, which is --hs2_http_port unless a proxy maps a different port. Impala handles the requests to the path of the URL as SAML responses.

section.p: The client starts the authentication, and Impala and the client use the following steps:

ol.li: The client opens a local port, and it sends a request to the HiveServer2 HTTP endpoint with the X-Hive-Token-Response-Port header set to that port. Impala answers with a redirect to the IdP, and with a client identifier in the X-Hive-Client-Identifier header.
The client opens the redirect URL in a browser. The user signs in at the IdP, and the IdP posts the SAML response to the callback URL.
Impala validates the response and returns a page that sends a bearer token to the local port of the client. If the validation fails, the page contains an error message instead of the token.
The client sends the requests again with the X-Hive-Client-Identifier header and the Authorization: Bearer header with the token. Impala validates the token and returns an authentication cookie.
The client uses the cookie in the next requests.

section.p: The token is valid for the time that --saml2_callback_token_ttl sets, 30000 milliseconds by default, and it can be used only once. The user must finish the sign-in within 5 minutes, because Impala keeps the state of the sign-in in the memory of the coordinator for that time. Therefore the IdP must post the response to the coordinator that started the sign-in. The lifetime of the cookie is controlled by --max_cookie_lifetime_s, and the cookies are valid on more than one coordinator only if you configure the same --cookie_secret_file for them. See .

The client must implement the protocol above, which is the SAML2 browser flow of HiveServer2. impala-shell does not support SAML2 authentication. You can use SAML2 together with Kerberos or LDAP on the HiveServer2 HTTP endpoint: a request that does not start the SAML2 flow is authenticated with the other methods that you configured. This combination is experimental. If a client starts the SAML2 flow and fails, Impala returns the HTTP status 401 and does not try the other methods.
